title: MESH diagnostics, version 1
description: What `mesh check --format json` prints on stdout: one document, on one line, holding every diagnostic of the run in the order MESH reports them. This schema lists exactly the properties this MESH prints. A later MESH may add properties without changing `version`, so consumers should ignore properties they don't know rather than validate against an older copy of this schema.

code.description: The diagnostic's stable code, in kebab-case. A code is never renamed or reused for a different meaning; new codes may be added.

message.description: A human-readable message. It may change between versions; match on `code`, not on this.

path.description: The file the span points into, exactly as it was passed on the command line: the `.mprx` file, or the `--model` manifest for a `manifest-*` code.

suggestions.description: Replacements that would probably fix the problem, best first. Usually empty.

replacement.description: The text to put in place of `span`.

span.description: A source range: `start` is its first character, and `end` is just past its last.

byte.description: A 0-based byte offset into the file's UTF-8 text, a byte-order mark included.

column.description: The 1-based column, counting Unicode scalar values from the start of the line. A byte-order mark and a line's `\r` are not columns.

utf16.description: A 0-based offset in UTF-16 code units into the file's text, the one that corresponds to `byte`: what a JavaScript string holding the same text indexes, as in `source.slice(start.utf16, end.utf16)`. A byte-order mark counts, as one unit.

utf16Column.description: The 1-based column, counting UTF-16 code units from the start of the line, with `column`'s rules: a byte-order mark and a line's `\r` are not columns.
